authoredPrompt: This figure is a plain vector diagram of four arrows stacked one above another, all drawn at the same shallow upward slope so their lengths can be compared at a glance. Each arrow starts from a small filled black dot. The topmost arrow, in dark navy, is by far the longest and is labeled 3v at its head. Below it an orange arrow labeled v runs in the same up-and-to-the-right direction at about a third that length. Beneath the orange one, a teal arrow labeled 1/2 v is half as long as v and again points the same way. The bottom arrow, drawn in red and labeled -v, has its dot at the right end and its arrowhead at the left, so it runs down and to the left while staying parallel to the others and matching v in length. Because all four share a single line of action, the only difference the eye registers is length, plus the reversal in the last one. The arrangement gives the geometric reading of multiplying a vector by a scalar: a positive factor stretches or shrinks the arrow while preserving its heading, and a negative factor turns it back on itself.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for scalar multiplier k: the learner drags k from negative to positive values, the arrow length scales and flips direction when k crosses 0, and scalar multiplication is seen as stretching, shrinking, or reversing a vector.
- Toggle between stacked comparison and overlay: the learner switches from separate arrows to all arrows sharing the same tail, the endpoints line up by scale factor, and equal direction for positive multiples versus opposite direction for negative multiples becomes easier to read.
authoredContext:
See the figure for a geometric interpretation. If v =〈 3,1 〉, then

Showing the effect of scaling a vector: 3x, 1x,.5x, and -1x. The 3x is three times as long, the 1x stays the same, the.5x halves the length, and the -1x reverses the direction of the vector but keeps the length the same. The rest keep the same direction; only the magnitude changes.

discrepancies: the default vector arrangement is very close, but the generated figure has substantial extra horizontal padding and a taller canvas compared with the tight source crop
the half-vector label is rendered as a compact single-line '½v' rather than the source's stacked fraction '1/2' over the v
the interactive slider's negative values in the default stacked view draw the changing vector up-left instead of down-left, so the dynamic negative scalar example is not opposite to v
the rendered output includes a large right-side control panel that is not part of the source image and visually changes the drop-in static composition
evaluation.notes: The static default vectors, colors, and labels are largely faithful, but the negative-scalar slider behavior is conceptually wrong and the half-vector label/crop differ from the source.
action_items: Fix currentStackEnds(k) for k < 0 so the dynamic vector endpoint is down-left from its shifted tail, matching the true direction of −v.
Render the half-vector label as a stacked fraction with 1 over 2 followed by v, matching the source typography more closely.
Adjust the SVG aspect ratio/crop or preserveAspectRatio settings so the figure fills the image area like the source without large horizontal padding.
Consider docking or minimizing controls so the default visual reads more like the original static figure when first loaded.
